summary: Configured persistent inventory log forwarding from node2 to node1. Messages tagged `inventory` are delivered over TCP and stored at `/var/log/inventory/node2.log`. End-to-end flow and retained data were verified after restarting each node individually.
actions_performed: Configured node1 rsyslog to listen on TCP/514 and accept inventory-tagged messages from node2.
Configured node2 rsyslog with a persistent disk-assisted forwarding queue and unlimited retry.
Verified the destination file is owned by syslog:adm with mode 0640.
Restarted node1 and node2 sequentially using native systemd reboot scheduling.
Confirmed changed boot IDs, recovered services, retained records, and successful post-restart delivery.

evidence.requirement: Forward inventory logs from node2 to node1 and persist them under /var/log/inventory/node2.log
evidence.summary: Both configurations validated; node2 established a TCP connection and the exact pre-restart inventory marker appeared in the required node1 file.
node1 boot ID changed from 17b362d1-c234-4169-bc4e-114d01fdf401 to 5d9468c3-7a68-4d3f-9376-7537a9503ade. The listener recovered, existing data remained, and a new inventory marker arrived afterward.

node2 boot ID changed from 29011044-5356-46eb-ba9c-1470170355a7 to 7c21ee57-2a69-4769-8f68-ed0f6241bd6b. rsyslog recovered, re-established TCP forwarding, and node1 stored a new post-restart marker alongside both earlier records.
